added_failures_note: derived from the reviewed run's own two gate logs (gate/base-picker.txt at e22aa6f and gate/head-picker.txt at c2f7666): both arms report EXIT=0 with no FAILED or ERROR line (base 173 passed, head 179 passed), so 0 added. The reviewed manifest names these logs with the key 'log' inside prose rather than a 'log_path' field, so the store's own read-time annotator reports the count unmeasured for this run; the count recorded here was derived directly from the two logs.

findings.text: follow-on: _serving_lanes groups the offered candidates by family to name the lanes that can serve the node, but lane_context.lanes (reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:360-364) already groups the same candidates by the same family and publishes the result as the keys of the state's 'lanes' block, which build_state holds in scope as lane['lanes'] - in the golden fixture 'lanes' keys are ['f'] and serving_lanes is ['f'], the same set. The two agree whenever every offered candidate names a family, so a second lane-grouping now exists where one was already derived.

follow-on: the reviewed manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite fields name their gate logs with the key 'log' inside prose, but the store's own annotator (reckon/crew/review.py:_gate_log_path) reads the field's JSON object or a 'log_path' line, so annotate_review_of_run resolves no log and reports the added-failure count unmeasured for this run - measured: read_review returns added_failure_count None and base_log_revision None though both logs exist at the paths the manifest's test_logs names. The baseline arm's own receipt (gate/base-picker.txt:2) compounds it: its command opens with a doubled interpreter prefix and spells its file set with the placeholder '<shared picker gate files + test_picker_helpers_have_one_owner.py>', so the base arm is not reproducible from its own header either.

follow-on: §19's done-when asks, when the state changed, for the replayed probability after the change; the manifest gives the two recorded probabilities (0.83, 0.84), their verdicts and the added fields, but states no replayed probability after the change, so the post-change outcome is shown by the lane facts rather than by a probability figure.

follow-on: the three new keys (serving_lanes, serving_lane_count, hold_waits_for) are added inside the 'local_lane' block, whose name scopes its other contents (admission, running, headroom, worker_slots) to the local lane, while these describe every lane that can serve the node - the golden fixture renders serving_lanes as ['f'], which is not the local lane - so the block's name and its new contents disagree.

item_verdicts.diff: One commit, c2f7666 'feat(picker): name the lanes that can serve the rendered node', over base e22aa6f. It adds the _GLOSSARY entries serving_lanes and hold_waits_for, the helpers _serving_lanes and _hold_waits_for, the three new local_lane keys in build_state, the new test file, and the regenerated GOLDEN_STATE fixture. No production module other than prompts.py is touched.
item_verdicts.done_when: §19's done-when asks the manifest to give the replayed hold probability and its verdict with the lane figures that decide it, and, because the state changed, the replayed probability after the change; a test must prove the rendered state names the single serving lane. The manifest gives both recorded probabilities (0.83, 0.84), their verdict (both 'hold was wrong'), the deciding lane figures (7 of 8 backends review-excluded, native also in-harness, one lane left) and the added fields, and the test proves the single serving lane; it does not give a replayed probability after the change.

The third is outside the declared scope and is declared as a deviation in the manifest; snapshot.py, a §19 write path, is untouched.

justifications.durability: The change is genuinely guarded: removing the three local_lane fields reddens 4 tests of tests/test_hold_names_the_serving_lane.py including both parametrised recorded-hold cases (gate-neg-repro.log, EXIT=1), so a regression that dropped the fact fails rather than passing quietly. The tests assert the rendered value of the new fields across one serving lane, two serving lanes, none, and the glossary, so the count is not a constant. Not 20 because the family-to-backend fallback branch in _serving_lanes is exercised by no dedicated case.
justifications.evidence: I reproduced the head gate independently in a scratch tree extracted from c2f7666 (gate-head-repro.log, module reckon/crew/picker/prompts.py, 179 passed EXIT=0, equal to the run's own after_suite) and the negative control (removing the three fields reddens 4 tests, EXIT=1; gate-neg-repro.log), and derived added_failure_count=0 with added_failure_ids=[] from the reviewed run's own two gate logs via reckon.crew.review.added_failures_from_gate_logs, whose recorded revisions match base and head. Docked because the reviewed manifest names its gate logs with 'log' inside prose rather than a 'log_path' field, so the store's own annotator reports the count unmeasured for this run (read_review returns added_failure_count None and base_log_revision None), and because the baseline arm's recorded command (gate/base-picker.txt:2) is malformed - a doubled interpreter prefix and a '<shared picker gate files + test_picker_helpers_have_one_owner.py>' placeholder - so the base arm is not reproducible from its own receipt; and because the manifest does not give the done-when's replayed probability after the state change.
justifications.fit: The new helpers and glossary entries are named for their mechanism (_serving_lanes, _hold_waits_for, serving_lanes, hold_waits_for) with no plan, stage or ticket label and no author attribution, matching the module's existing private-helper idiom and docstring style. Docked because the three keys are placed inside the 'local_lane' block, whose name scopes its contents to the local lane, while serving_lanes and serving_lane_count describe every lane that can serve the node - the golden fixture renders them as ['f'], not the local lane.
justifications.goal_fidelity: §19's goal is that the rendered state name, per node, how many lanes can serve it and what a hold waits on. At head c2f7666 reckon/crew/picker/prompts.py:254-256 adds serving_lanes, serving_lane_count and hold_waits_for to the state's local_lane block, derived from the offered candidates pick() passes (reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:306 keeps only candidates with no reasons, :327 passes them to render), and the new test asserts serving_lanes == ['local'] and holding_waits_for == 'the local lane, the only lane that can serve this node' for both recorded holds; I reproduced that at head (gate-head-repro.log: 179 passed). The one thing left to the model rather than asserted is the weight it puts on the fact.
justifications.reuse: reckon/crew/picker/prompts.py:165 _serving_lanes re-derives the distinct lane names (candidates grouped by family) that lane_context.lanes already produces as the keys of the state's own 'lanes' block (reckon/crew/picker/lane_context.py:360-364 groups the same candidates by the same key), and build_state already holds that block in scope as lane['lanes'] - the golden fixture renders 'lanes' == {'f': {...}} and serving_lanes == ['f'], the same set. The two groupings differ only in _serving_lanes' fallback to candidate.backend when family is absent, a case no offered candidate in the tests exhibits. A second lane-grouping where the state already carries one.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --name-only e22aa6f c2f7666 lists exactly four paths: reckon/crew/picker/prompts.py, tests/test_hold_names_the_serving_lane.py, tests/test_picker_helpers_have_one_owner.py and the evidence fragment. Three are inside the node's declared scope (prompts.py and its tests); the golden rendered-state fixture tests/test_picker_helpers_have_one_owner.py is outside the declared write scope and is declared as a deviation - the fixture pins the exact rendered bytes, so adding the fields necessarily moved them, and the change is a faithful regeneration from the head tree over the frozen fixture (only the three new keys differ in GOLDEN_STATE). §19's declared write paths also name reckon/crew/picker/snapshot.py, which is left untouched and needed no change.
